html:
Antioch was a great city on the Orontes River near the Mediterranean coast, in what is now southern Turkey, where the modern city of Antakya stands. For a thousand years it was one of the leading cities of the eastern Mediterranean.

Seleucus I founded it around 300 BCE, and it became the capital of the Seleucid Empire. Under the Roman Empire from 64 BCE it was the capital of Syria and one of the three largest cities of the empire. Followers of Jesus were first called Christians there, and Paul set out from it on his journeys. It became the seat of one of the great patriarchs of the church.

Its later history was hard:

  • The earthquake of 526 killed a huge number of people.
  • The Persian king Khosrow I sacked it in 540, breaking the Perpetual Peace.
  • It fell in the Arab conquests in 637, was retaken by the Byzantines in 969, and lost again to the Seljuks in 1084.
  • The First Crusade took it in 1098 after a long siege, on the road to Jerusalem, and it was the capital of a crusader principality until the Mamluks destroyed it in 1268.

It never recovered its old size. It became part of Turkey in 1939, and the earthquakes of 2023 left much of Antakya in ruins.
sum: Antioch was a great city on the Orontes River near the Mediterranean coast, in what is now southern Turkey, where the modern city of Antakya stands. For a thousand years it was one of the leading cities of the eastern Mediterranean.
